metaData.title: A Comprehensive Codex Practical Guide: The Most Complete Tutorial Online
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article is a comprehensive practical guide to OpenAI Codex, systematically covering its three main entry points, permission modes, best practices, prompt strategies, version management, context management, long-term memory, Skills, Plugins, MCP, and automation, along with complete engineering practice examples and common command templates.
metaData.summary: This article is a practical tutorial on OpenAI Codex aimed at programmers, helping developers systematically master how to use Codex. It first introduces the three main entry points: CLI, App, and IDE plugins, offering selection recommendations for different user groups. Then, it delves into key considerations for using Codex, including permission modes (default, auto-review, full access) and their applicable scenarios and risk controls. In the best practices section, the author proposes a four-step workflow: 'specify scope, specify status, specify acceptance criteria, and interrupt anytime,' emphasizing the relationship between prompt quality and token consumption. The article also details Codex's multimodal capabilities, version management, context management strategies, and advanced features like AGENTS.md for long-term memory, Skills, Plugins, MCP, and automation. Finally, through a complete Pomodoro timer application case, it demonstrates the full engineering practice from requirement breakdown to code implementation, review, fixing, and summarization, along with several practical command templates.

mainPoints.point: Using Codex should follow a stable workflow: 'read first, then plan, then execute, then verify, then summarize.'
mainPoints.explanation: A common mistake for beginners is giving a vague task and expecting AI to complete it in one go. The correct approach is to first let AI read the project structure, formulate a plan, then make small iterative changes, test and verify, and finally summarize and solidify experience by writing common rules into AGENTS.md.

mainPoints.point: Permission modes are key safety controls for using Codex and should be chosen based on task risk.
mainPoints.explanation: Default permissions are safest but require frequent confirmation; auto-review is suitable for daily continuous tasks and can automatically pass safe operations; full access offers the most power but carries the highest risk, suitable only for temporary use and should be switched back to a safer mode afterward.

mainPoints.point: Prompt quality directly impacts token consumption and output quality; short commands do not necessarily save tokens.
mainPoints.explanation: Vague short commands cause AI to guess and fill in context on its own, consuming more tokens instead. A more effective approach is to specify the exact scope, status, and acceptance criteria, allowing AI to work within clear constraints.

mainPoints.point: AGENTS.md is a key tool for solidifying project norms and team standards, enabling long-term memory.
mainPoints.explanation: Place AGENTS.md in the project root or subdirectory, writing rules about tech stack, code style, testing standards, directory conventions, etc. Codex will automatically read and follow these rules each time it enters the project, avoiding repeated explanations.

mainPoints.point: Skills and Plugins are core to extending Codex's capabilities, but building a solid foundation should come first.
mainPoints.explanation: Skills are methods of doing things, while Plugins are toolboxes. Beginners should first master basics like project reading/writing, permissions, context, AGENTS.md, and Git workflow, then gradually explore advanced features like MCP and automation.

keyQuotes: AI is not a god. It is an extremely powerful tool. But the more powerful the tool, the more you need to know how to use it.
In the context of Vibe Coding, the biggest fear is letting AI run wild.
Read first. Then plan. Then execute. Then verify. Then summarize. This is the simplest and most stable Codex workflow.
Many people run into problems with Codex because they don't clearly define the boundaries.
If you don't give acceptance criteria, it will just finish based on its own understanding. And AI's 'I think it's done' is often not the same as 'it's truly done' in engineering.
